To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the trophic structure of soil communities does not buffer the effect of drought on soil carbon cycling and microbial communities.
drought has a stronger effect than food web trophicity on soil processes related to carbon transfer from plants to the soil.
drought decreases the incorporation of recent plant-derived carbon into soil food webs, regardless of their trohic complexity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental question of ecology: How does the trophic structure of food webs influence their stability?

a fundamental process of ecosystem functioning and its response to global change, and provides new insight into the role of trophic complexity on soil functioning and its potential to buffer against global change impacts.
the question of how the trophic structure of soil food webs modulates the response of soil functions and microbial communities to drought.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
drought has a greater impact than food web complexity on carbon cycling in soil, and that the trophic level of the soil community does not buffer the effects of drought.
the effects of drought on soil food webs are not mitigated by trophic complexity, and that trophic complexity does not affect drought responses.
the trophic structure of soil food webs does not influence the effect of drought on soil functions and carbon transfer below‐ ground.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

soil food web trophi complexity does not affect soil functions in interaction with drought, and drought has a strong negative effect on the capture and transfer of recent photosynthates by plants to soil food webs.
drought has a greater effect on soil functions than does food web complexity.

drought decreases the incorporation of recent plant carbon into soil food webs and the trophic structure of the soil food web is not important to mitigate the effects of drought on the soil carbon cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
drought has strong negative effects on soil functions and microbial communities, and that these effects are not mitigated by the complexity of soil food webs.

drought has a stronger effect on soil functions than the trophic level complexity of soil food webs, and that the transfer of recent photosynthates to the below‐ground compartment is particularly sensitive to drought.
drought has strong effects on the flow of carbon from plants to soil food webs and that these effects are not buffered by the trophical complexity of soil communities.
